title: AI Chatbots in Chinese higher education: adoption, perception, and influence among graduate students—an integrated analysis utilizing UTAUT and ECM models
extended_summary:
This paper examines what drives Chinese graduate students’ acceptance, satisfaction, behavioral intention, and use of AI chatbots in higher education. The authors aim to understand which factors best explain continued use of AI chatbot tools by integrating two established technology-adoption frameworks: the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM). The study is framed around students’ adoption of tools such as ChatGPT and similar AI chatbots for learning and research, rather than evaluating learning outcomes or writing-quality effects.

The approach is a survey-based correlational study using self-reported questionnaire data from 373 master’s and doctoral students across multiple Chinese universities. Data were collected over a two-week period through the Wenjuanxing platform and analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The model included constructs such as performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, confirmation, satisfaction, personal innovativeness, behavioral intention, and use behavior.

The study context is Chinese higher education, specifically graduate students using AI chatbots for study and research tasks. Participants were mostly master’s students, with both male and female respondents, and the sample was drawn from several universities in China. The paper discusses AI chatbots broadly, including ChatGPT, Bing, Notion AI, and Chinese tools such as Wenxin Yiyan, as technologies that may support academic work.

The main conclusion is that ECM-related variables—especially confirmation and satisfaction—were stronger predictors of continued AI chatbot use than most UTAUT variables. Performance expectancy and personal innovativeness positively predicted behavioral intention, while satisfaction was a major driver of intended continued use. Effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions did not significantly predict behavioral intention, and facilitating conditions did not significantly predict use behavior. The paper concludes that graduate students’ continued use of AI chatbots depends more on whether the tools meet expectations and generate satisfaction than on external social pressures or perceived infrastructure support.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational survey study using PLS-SEM with a reasonably sized sample (n=373), but it is not an experiment and does not estimate causal effects on learning outcomes. It meets limited credibility criteria through transparent methods and validated constructs, but lacks a counterfactual design.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports statistically significant associations for adoption- and perception-related outcomes, but not direct causal impacts on writing quality or other academic outcomes, and reported effects are mostly path coefficients from a usage model rather than intervention effect sizes. Impact is therefore modest or unclear for education outcomes relevant to the K-12 writing-feedback topic.

interventions.use_case: Survey study of graduate students' adoption, satisfaction, behavioral intention, and self-reported use frequency of AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Bing, Notion AI, and Wenxin Yiyan for learning and research tasks in higher education.

finding.finding_summary: Among 373 Chinese graduate students, satisfaction with AI chatbots for learning and research was a significant positive predictor of behavioral intention to continue using them (path coefficient β=0.059, t=6.408, p<0.001). Satisfaction itself was positively associated with performance expectancy (β=0.419, t=8.532, p<0.001), effort expectancy (β=0.285, t=6.289, p<0.001), and confirmation (β=0.194, t=4.065, p<0.001), indicating more favorable attitudes and user satisfaction when expectations were met.
finding.measure: Self-reported satisfaction, confirmation, and behavioral intention scales derived from UTAUT/ECM using 7-point Likert items
finding.effect_size: β=0.059 for Satisfaction→Behavioral Intention; β=0.419 for Performance Expectancy→Satisfaction; β=0.285 for Effort Expectancy→Satisfaction; β=0.194 for Confirmation→Satisfaction

finding.finding_summary: The study found that perceived performance benefits of AI chatbots for study and research were positively related to continued intention to use them (β=0.203, t=2.917, p=0.004). Participants reported moderately high agreement that chatbots helped them complete tasks and projects faster and increased productivity, though these were perception-based indicators rather than objective productivity measures.
finding.measure: Self-reported performance expectancy/productivity items and behavioral intention to use AI chatbots

finding.finding_summary: The paper provides evidence that graduate student adoption of AI chatbots in Chinese higher education is shaped more by expectation confirmation and satisfaction than by social influence or facilitating conditions. Social influence did not significantly predict behavioral intention (β=0.059, t=0.874, p=0.382), and facilitating conditions did not significantly predict behavioral intention (β=0.051, t=0.909, p=0.364) or use behavior (β=0.109, t=1.949, p=0.051), suggesting institutional support and peer norms were less important than user experience in this sample.
finding.measure: Structural equation model paths for social influence, facilitating conditions, behavioral intention, and self-reported use behavior
finding.effect_size: β=0.059 for Social Influence→Behavioral Intention; β=0.051 for Facilitating Conditions→Behavioral Intention; β=0.109 for Facilitating Conditions→Use Behavior
